speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam
text: asked the Minister for Law (a) in what ways are press reports of on-going trials of sex crimes regulated; and (b) what protection is there for medical professionals whose reputations are affected by media coverage of on-going trials of sex crimes.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: In this, we look at the practice in other jurisdictions.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The second approach is to lean in favour of just having open court proceedings and all matters are out immediately.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: There is no general power to the courts to grant accused persons any sort of anonymity to protect their reputations.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: For example, in the United Kingdom, the general position is that legal proceedings should be held in public and there are some rules, exceptions which restrict media reporting of some criminal cases, which prohibit the disclosure of identity of accused persons.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: But the primary aim of those provisions is to protect vulnerable witnesses and victims, and to avoid substantial risk of prejudicing proceedings, if such a risk exists.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: I think Dr Tan's question probably arises from the trials of doctors for sex crimes, but it applies to all accused in a variety of cases.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: That also allows unidentified victims of serial offenders, for example, to come forward and seek help.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: But I emphasise that our position on this issue is not set in concrete.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: I would say that even in the current situation, in certain circumstances, there is anonymity given if it is required for public interest.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: For example, to sensitive information relating to national security or if the release of information on the accused may lead to identification of, say, children, young persons and alleged victims of sexual or child abuse offences.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The reason for doing that is to protect those vulnerable victims and children from being identified and give them a better life.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: With that focus, the Courts have some power to prohibit publication of the identity of the accused and impose some conditions on how the trial can be reported and the media have got to comply with those requirements.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: There are, as I said, pros and cons with both approaches – whether to allow or to prohibit the publication of names of accused persons until they are convicted.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: And as I said earlier, we will keep our position under view.
